IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF ILLINOIS
EASTERN DIVISION

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

                    Plaintiff,

     v.                                    Civil Action No. 1:26-cv-02219

HALVORSEN PLATING WORKS, INC.,
and CLAUDIA HALVORSEN-REYES,

                    Defendants.

CONSENT JUDGMENT AND ORDER

WHEREAS, Plaintiff the United States of America, on behalf of the United States Environmental Protection Agency, filed a Complaint on March 3, 2026 alleging that Defendants discharged pollutants from their electroplating facility at 4400 South Kedzie Avenue, Chicago, Illinois into the publicly owned treatment works in violation of Sections 307(d) and 309 of the Clean Water Act, 33 U.S.C. §§ 1317(d) and 1319, and the pretreatment standards at 40 C.F.R. Part 433;

WHEREAS, Defendants deny the allegations of the Complaint and this Consent Judgment is not an admission of liability or of any fact alleged, except as necessary to establish this Court's jurisdiction;

WHEREAS, the Parties agree that settlement of this matter without further litigation is in the public interest and is a fair, reasonable, and appropriate means of resolving the claims alleged; and

WHEREAS, the Parties have negotiated this Consent Judgment in good faith and at arm's length;

NOW, THEREFORE, with the consent of the Parties, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, ADJUDGED, AND DECREED as follows:

1. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

1.1 This Court has jurisdiction over the subject matter under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 1345, and 1355 and Section 309(b) of the Clean Water Act, 33 U.S.C. § 1319(b), and over the Parties. Venue is proper in this District under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) and Section 309(b) because the violations occurred in this District.

1.2 Defendants consent to this Court's jurisdiction over them and over the subject matter, and waive any objection to venue, solely for the purposes of entry and enforcement of this Consent Judgment.

2. APPLICABILITY

2.1 This Consent Judgment binds the United States and Defendants, and Defendants' officers, directors, agents, successors, and assigns, and any person acting in concert with them who receives actual notice of it.

2.2 Defendants shall provide a copy of this Consent Judgment to each officer and employee whose duties relate to compliance with it, and to any contractor performing work required by it, within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date.

2.3 No transfer of ownership of the facility relieves Defendants of any obligation. At least thirty (30) days before any transfer, Defendants shall notify the United States and shall provide the transferee a copy of this Consent Judgment.

3. INJUNCTIVE RELIEF

3.1 Defendants shall achieve and maintain compliance with the pretreatment standards at 40 C.F.R. Part 433 and with their discharge permit.

3.2 Within one hundred eighty (180) days after the Effective Date, Defendants shall install and place into operation the chromium reduction and pH adjustment system described in Appendix A, and shall certify completion to the United States within fourteen (14) days after startup.

3.3 Within ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, Defendants shall submit to the United States for review and approval a written Operation and Maintenance Plan and a Slug Discharge Control Plan meeting the requirements of Appendix B.

3.4 Beginning with the first full calendar quarter after the Effective Date, Defendants shall sample the regulated discharge weekly, using the methods at 40 C.F.R. Part 136, and shall retain the results for five (5) years.

4. CIVIL PENALTY

4.1 Defendants shall pay a civil penalty of $685,000, jointly and severally, within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, by FedWire transfer to the United States Department of Justice in accordance with instructions the United States provides.

4.2 The penalty is not deductible for federal tax purposes, and Defendants shall not claim it as a deduction.

4.3 If any portion is not paid when due, Defendants shall pay interest under 28 U.S.C. § 1961, a handling charge, and a six percent (6%) per year penalty charge on the unpaid balance, and the United States may pursue any available collection remedy.

5. REPORTING

5.1 Defendants shall submit a semi-annual progress report by January 31 and July 31 of each year, describing the status of each requirement, all sampling results, and any violation of this Consent Judgment.

5.2 Defendants shall report any violation of this Consent Judgment or of the pretreatment standards to the United States within seven (7) days after discovery, and shall describe the cause and the corrective action taken.

5.3 Each submission shall be signed by a responsible corporate officer and shall bear the certification required by 40 C.F.R. § 122.22(d).

6. STIPULATED PENALTIES

6.1 For each day of failure to meet a deadline in Section 3, Defendants shall pay a stipulated penalty of $2,500 per day for days 1 through 30, $5,000 per day for days 31 through 60, and $10,000 per day thereafter.

6.2 For each late or deficient report under Section 5, Defendants shall pay $1,000 per day.

6.3 Stipulated penalties accrue without demand and are due within thirty (30) days after the United States makes a written demand. The United States may reduce or waive any stipulated penalty in its unreviewable discretion.

7. FORCE MAJEURE

7.1 A "Force Majeure Event" is an event beyond Defendants' control that delays performance despite Defendants' best efforts. Increased cost, changed business circumstances, and the failure of a contractor Defendants selected are not Force Majeure Events.

7.2 Defendants shall notify the United States by telephone within seventy-two (72) hours and in writing within seven (7) days of any event they claim is a Force Majeure Event, and bear the burden of proving it. If the United States disagrees, Defendants may seek relief from the Court.

8. DISPUTE RESOLUTION

8.1 The Parties shall attempt informal resolution for twenty (20) days after written notice of a dispute. If informal resolution fails, Defendants may file a motion with this Court, and bear the burden of demonstrating that their position is consistent with this Consent Judgment and the Clean Water Act.

9. EFFECT OF SETTLEMENT AND RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

9.1 This Consent Judgment resolves the civil claims of the United States alleged in the Complaint through the date of lodging.

9.2 The United States reserves all other claims, including any claim for criminal liability, for imminent and substantial endangerment, and for violations occurring after the date of lodging.

9.3 This Consent Judgment does not limit the rights of any third party and confers no rights on any person other than the Parties.

10. COSTS, RETENTION OF JURISDICTION, AND TERMINATION

10.1 Each Party bears its own costs and attorneys' fees, except that the United States may recover the costs of collecting any unpaid amount.

10.2 This Court retains jurisdiction to enforce this Consent Judgment and to resolve any dispute arising under it.

10.3 Defendants may move to terminate this Consent Judgment after they have maintained compliance for twenty-four (24) consecutive months, have completed the injunctive relief, and have paid all penalties due. The United States may oppose the motion.

11. PUBLIC COMMENT AND ENTRY

11.1 The United States shall lodge this Consent Judgment with the Court for at least thirty (30) days for public comment under 28 C.F.R. § 50.7, and may withdraw or withhold consent if the comments disclose facts showing that it is inappropriate, improper, or inadequate.

11.2 The "Effective Date" is the date this Court enters this Consent Judgment.

SO ORDERED.

Dated: ____________________          ____________________________
                                     United States District Judge
